product_relevance.what_product_question_it_informs: The size of the publicly reachable remote-access surface, as an infrastructure-exposure signal and a proxy for deployment footprint.
product_relevance.weakest_truthful_interpretation: A count of addresses that completed a TCP handshake on one port. It is a PROXY for exposure and is not adoption, demand, willingness to pay or market size.
product_relevance.why_it_is_weaker_than_it_looks: A port that accepts a connection tells you nothing about what is listening. The relevance is exposure-surface, not protocol adoption, and §7 requires the weakest truthful reading.

proposition.observation_window_semantics: the probe time of the scan that produced the response, selectable before retrieval
proposition.predicate: a TCP SYN sent to port 22 received a positive response
proposition.inclusion_rule: an address is counted once if at least one positive SYN response on port 22 falls inside W
proposition.exclusion_rule: opted-out and unscanned addresses are outside the frame, not zeros
proposition.vantage_semantics: LOAD_BEARING AND ELEVATED. A port may respond from one scanner region and not another, and with no application response to corroborate it there is nothing in the record to detect a vantage-relative difference.
proposition.configuration_assumptions: port 22 must be inside the scanned port set of every apparatus counted, for the window

what_a_positive_observation_establishes: That at that moment, from that vantage, that address completed a TCP handshake on port 22.
explicit_non_claims: NOT that an SSH server is running — this is the single most important non-claim, and the construct must never be relabelled by the protocol conventionally assigned to the port
not that any protocol was spoken at all
not that a service is installed, deployed or in use
not a count of hosts, organisations, devices or customers
why_tcp_responsiveness_is_not_ssh: A SYN response is a transport-layer fact produced by the operating system's TCP stack. Nothing about it identifies the application listening on the port, and a port may be forwarded, honeypotted, firewalled-open or answered by an unrelated service. The SSH construct exists precisely because RFC 4253 §4.2 gives an application-layer discriminator, and the whole content of that discriminator is absent here.

Censys.note: A discovery stage separate from service identification IS documented — a global scan of popular ports followed by handshake attempts — which is the right stage for this predicate. What is not documented is whether the published surfaces represent a port that answered without producing a service, and the dated snapshot's schema is not public.

Netlas.note: The decisive question of this mission for Netlas. Its collection is named Responses, its documented fallback field stores an unparsed network RESPONSE, and no retrieved page states that a document exists for a port that accepted a connection and returned nothing. If it does not, Netlas counts a strict subset and §13 fails.

LeakIX.note: Global blocker, unaffected by the predicate.

Shadowserver.note: Global blocker, unaffected by the predicate.

ONYPHE.note: datascan is generated by a raw application response, and no held evidence describes any ONYPHE category publishing port-openness independent of a response.

Rapid7 Project Sonar.note: sonar.tcp publishes regular snapshots of responses to zmap probes against common TCP services, as dated immutable per-port CSV files whose names carry the date and the port, over a documented public-IPv4 frame with an explicit opt-out exclusion. This is the strongest single route the arc has produced.

Shodan.note: Global blocker, unaffected by the predicate.

unresolved_load_bearing_questions: what the date in a Sonar study filename denotes
whether a TCP/22 Sonar study file exists and for which windows
whether one Sonar CSV row is one address, so that a distinct-address count is not a row count
whether Netlas or Censys represents a port that answered without producing a service
failed_hard_conditions: at least TWO apparatus routes are PLAUSIBLE
how_close_it_came: This is the closest candidate. One route is not merely plausible but well documented, and the second is unresolved rather than blocked on two apparatuses. A single documented sentence about how a no-response open port is represented would move it.
